# v2 - Re-verify the meld

v1 returned REVISE with four blockers, thirteen majors and ten minors, and n9 and n10 meld them.
A meld of that size touches the same gate the review was about, so the green suite is not the
review. A fresh agent that wrote none of it reads the meld against v1's findings and against the
same criteria, and tries again to make the runner write `done` on something the code did not
verify.

This pass is narrower than v1. v1 covered the whole intent; v2 covers the meld and the parts of the
gate the meld moved.

## Criteria
- Every blocker v1 raised is closed by code, not by a test that asserts on its own fixture.
  Reproduce each of the four the way v1 did, against a real scratch repository, and confirm the new
  behaviour rather than the new test.
- The return's own `status:` governs. No path writes `done` from a return that said anything else,
  and no path pays for a merge or a suite on a return that said anything else.
- `plastic_home` resolves to a real installed manifest, proven against this machine's own
  installation rather than a fixture.
- An unmeasurable diff refuses. A verify node that commits anything fails scope.
- No transition is written by a session that does not hold the delivery lock, on any path into
  `step`.
- Every major v1 raised is either closed or explicitly recorded as dropped with a reason. Name any
  that were dropped.
- The meld introduced no new path that raises across the runner's boundary, and no new report that
  claims a check the code skipped.
- `gates=` names exactly the checks that ran, on every state the absorb can write.
- The matrices of n9 and n10 name tests that exist and that genuinely exercise the stated operation.
